question: Which of the following peptides are not produced by the renal system?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Renin" -> "produced by juxtaglomerular cells in kidneys" -> "part of renal system" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Angiotensin I" -> "produced by conversion of angiotensinogen by renin" -> "occurs in bloodstream" -> "not directly produced by renal system" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Erythropoietin" -> "produced by interstitial fibroblasts in kidneys" -> "part of renal system" -> 90%
CHAIN: "1,25DHCC" -> "active form of vitamin D" -> "converted in kidneys" -> "produced by renal system" -> 90%
analysis: To determine which peptide is not produced by the renal system, we need to evaluate each option based on their origin and production process. Renin is produced by the juxtaglomerular cells in the kidneys, making it a product of the renal system. Erythropoietin is produced by interstitial fibroblasts in the kidneys, also classifying it as a renal product. 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol (1,25DHCC), the active form of vitamin D, is synthesized in the kidneys, confirming its renal origin. Angiotensin I, however, is formed in the bloodstream through the action of renin on angiotensinogen, which is produced by the liver. Therefore, Angiotensin I is not directly produced by the renal system. Based on this analysis, Angiotensin I is the peptide not produced by the renal system.
